Compare two retrievals record by record

Source: R/diff_records.R
scopus_diff_records.Rd

Identifies which records were added, removed or unchanged between an earlier and a later retrieval, and gives each record's citation count in both. scopus_diff_dois() compares DOIs alone, and this function compares the records themselves, matched as scopus_combine(dedupe = TRUE) matches them. A record without a DOI is therefore still tracked by its 'Scopus' identifier, and two records under one DOI are not taken for one.

Usage

scopus_diff_records(old, new)

Arguments

old, new

scopus_records objects, or data frames with a scopus_id or a doi column, representing the earlier (old) and later (new) retrievals. The title, year and citations columns are read where present.

Value

A tibble of class scopus_record_diff, one row per record, with the columns status, scopus_id, doi, title, year, citations_old and citations_new. status is a factor with levels "added" (in new only), "removed" (in old only), "conflict" (see Details) and "unchanged" (in both). Rows are sorted by status, then DOI, identifier and title, in byte order, so the order is the same under every locale and in the Python twin. The integer attributes n_old_without_id_or_doi and n_new_without_id_or_doi count the records on each side that carried neither key and so were not compared. Printing shows the counts in each category, and those records where there are any.

Details

Two records are one record when they share a 'Scopus' identifier, or when they share a DOI and one of them lacks an identifier. DOIs are compared as scopus_extract_dois() compares them, without resolver prefixes and ignoring case. Records with different identifiers are never matched, even under one DOI, since 'Scopus' gives one DOI to distinct papers as well as holding duplicate records of one paper (scopus_combine() gives the sources).

A record found in one retrieval only is a "conflict" where the other retrieval gives its DOI to a different record. It may have been re-indexed under a new identifier, or it may be a distinct paper sharing the DOI. Only the two records themselves can tell, so it is counted neither as added nor as removed. A record without an identifier whose DOI two identified records carry is in the same position. A record with neither an identifier nor a DOI cannot be matched at all, and is left out of the rows and counted.

scopus_id is the identifier the record was matched on, missing for a record matched on its DOI alone. doi is the DOI without its resolver prefix, in the case the record gives it. doi, title and year come from the later retrieval where it holds the record and gives a value, and from the earlier one otherwise, while citations_old and citations_new come from each retrieval in turn. Where one retrieval holds a record more than once, the first value it gives is used.

See also

scopus_diff_dois() to compare DOIs alone, scopus_combine() to merge the retrievals.

Examples

# The bundled corpus carries no 'Scopus' identifiers, so its records are
# matched on their DOIs, and the eleven in each pull without one cannot be
# compared at all.
baseline <- example_records[example_records$year <= 2023, ]
later <- example_records[-1, ]
scopus_diff_records(old = baseline, new = later)
#> <scopus_record_diff> 14 added, 1 removed, 0 in conflict, 112 unchanged, 11
#> earlier and 11 later records without an identifier or a DOI not compared
#> # A tibble: 127 × 7
#>    status scopus_id doi                  title  year citations_old citations_new
#>    <fct>  <chr>     <chr>                <chr> <int>         <int>         <int>
#>  1 added  NA        10.1002/adfm.202315… Vasc…  2024            NA            32
#>  2 added  NA        10.1002/asia.202400… A Hi…  2024            NA             6
#>  3 added  NA        10.1002/slct.202302… Allo…  2024            NA             2
#>  4 added  NA        10.1016/j.cej.2024.… High…  2024            NA            31
#>  5 added  NA        10.1016/j.diamond.2… Copp…  2024            NA            21
#>  6 added  NA        10.1016/j.isci.2024… Boos…  2024            NA             8
#>  7 added  NA        10.1016/j.jallcom.2… Enha…  2024            NA             5
#>  8 added  NA        10.1016/j.jallcom.2… From…  2024            NA            84
#>  9 added  NA        10.1016/j.jpowsour.… How …  2024            NA            14
#> 10 added  NA        10.1016/j.jpowsour.… High…  2024            NA             3
#> # ℹ 117 more rows

# Two pulls of three records each, with identifiers as a live harvest
# carries them. 10.5555 is the DOI prefix reserved for tests, so none of
# these resolve. The later pull holds 10.5555/c under a new identifier,
# which makes both records under it a conflict to check, and a record from
# another source, without an identifier, that is new.
old <- data.frame(
  scopus_id = c("85000000001", "85000000002", "85000000003"),
  doi = c("10.5555/a", "10.5555/b", "10.5555/c"),
  citations = c(5L, 3L, 8L)
)
new <- data.frame(
  scopus_id = c("85000000001", "85000000033", NA),
  doi = c("10.5555/a", "10.5555/c", "https://doi.org/10.5555/D"),
  citations = c(9L, 10L, NA)
)
scopus_diff_records(old, new)
#> <scopus_record_diff> 1 added, 1 removed, 2 in conflict, 1 unchanged
#> # A tibble: 5 × 7
#>   status    scopus_id   doi       title  year citations_old citations_new
#>   <fct>     <chr>       <chr>     <chr> <int>         <int>         <int>
#> 1 added     NA          10.5555/D NA       NA            NA            NA
#> 2 removed   85000000002 10.5555/b NA       NA             3            NA
#> 3 conflict  85000000003 10.5555/c NA       NA             8            NA
#> 4 conflict  85000000033 10.5555/c NA       NA            NA            10
#> 5 unchanged 85000000001 10.5555/a NA       NA             5             9
